collect.bio: Bruno Retailleau (born 20 November 1960 in Cholet) is a conservative politician from the Vendée, senator since 2004 and president of Les Républicains since May 2025. He chaired the Vendée departmental council and the Pays de la Loire region, led the LR Senate group, and served as Interior Minister in the Barnier and Bayrou governments (Sept 2024 - Oct 2025). He declared his 2027 presidential candidacy in February 2026 and won the LR nomination on 19 April 2026. He is known for a restrictive line on immigration and security and for socially conservative positions.

reversals.topic: Participation in a government with Macron's camp
reversals.before: In 2022 he refused any coalition or governing deal with Macron's Renaissance party.
reversals.after: In September 2024 he joined the Barnier government as Interior Minister, a centrist-aligned coalition.

delivery.what: Anti-narcotics plan and legislation (national anti-narcotics prosecutor's office, informant status reform); law adopted April 2025
delivery.assessment: Presented jointly with Justice Minister Migaud and drawing on a Senate inquiry. Left-leaning senator Carlotti (Public Sénat) criticised his remarks on cutting social aid and the lack of funding for staff. Evidence on outcomes is thin in the sources I could open.

delivery.what: Immigration enforcement: bilateral return agreements (Morocco, Iraq, Kazakhstan, Egypt), pressure on prefects to speed up removals, revision of the Valls regularisation circular
delivery.assessment: Supporters count this as tougher enforcement. Critics inside the Macron camp objected to his tone, including the 'rule of law is neither absolute nor sacred' remark. Source is a Wikipedia summary, so figures on actual removals are not verified.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not directly verified: Libération and Le Monde could not be fetched. Opponents quoted via Wikipedia call his statements discriminatory, citing the 2023 'Français de papier' remark.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not verified: no right-leaning outlet could be fetched. Expected to frame him as a firm law-and-order figure, but this is an assumption.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Public Sénat coverage (Nov 2024) is procedural and reports both the minister's plan and a senator's criticism of it.

verify.bio: Bruno Retailleau (born 20 November 1960 in Cholet) is a conservative politician from the Vendée and has been president of Les Républicains since May 2025. He was senator for Vendée from 2004 to 2024 and again from November 2025. He chaired the Vendée departmental council (2010-2015) and the Pays de la Loire region (2015-2017), led the LR group in the Senate (2014-2024), and was Interior Minister in the Barnier, Bayrou and short-lived Lecornu I governments (September 2024 - October 2025). He declared his 2027 presidential candidacy on 12 February 2026 and was designated LR candidate after the party vote of 19 April 2026. He is known for a restrictive line on immigration and security and for socially conservative positions.

reversals.before: In 2022 he refused any governing agreement with Macron's Renaissance party, saying the right is 'not soluble in Macronism'.
reversals.after: In September 2024 he became Interior Minister in Michel Barnier's government, a coalition of LR and the presidential camp, and stayed under Bayrou; he left in October 2025 over the composition of the Lecornu government.

delivery.what: Anti-narcotics plan (announced November 2024 with Justice Minister Migaud) and backing for the Senate bill 'sortir la France du piège du narcotrafic' (Blanc/Durain): creation of a national anti-organised-crime prosecutor's office (PNACO) and reform of informant status. Adopted on 29 April 2025 and promulgated on 13 June 2025.
delivery.assessment: The law came from a cross-party Senate bill. Retailleau defended it, at first with Justice Minister Darmanin. It passed the Senate unanimously and the Assembly 396-68. The Conseil constitutionnel struck down the algorithmic-intelligence provisions. Socialist senator Carlotti backed the core measures but criticised his remarks on cutting social benefits and the lack of funding (Public Sénat). Evidence on outcomes is not covered in the sources read.

delivery.what: Immigration enforcement: negotiations with Iraq, Kazakhstan and Egypt on removals were announced (8 Oct 2024), along with an arrangement with Morocco to speed up returns (29 Oct 2024). A circular of 29 Oct 2024 asked prefects for 'complète mobilisation' on removals, and he announced the end of the Valls regularisation circular (Oct 2024). He also took a firm line with Algeria on readmissions.
delivery.assessment: Supporters see this as tougher enforcement. Critics inside the presidential camp objected to his remark that the rule of law is neither 'intangible' nor 'sacré'. The sources are Wikipedia summaries, so the agreements' contents and actual removal figures are not verified.

media_portrayal.left_media: Not directly verified: Libération, Mediapart and L'Humanité were not read. The secondary sources read report that his 2023 'Français de papier' remark and his rule-of-law comment drew wide criticism from opponents.
media_portrayal.right_media: Not verified: no right-leaning outlet was read, so no characterisation is given.
media_portrayal.neutral_media: Public Sénat (Nov 2024) reports his narcotics plan procedurally and gives room to a Socialist senator's partial support and criticism.

verify.sources_note: WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted), so verification relied on WebFetch reads of French and English Wikipedia (secondary, centre/neutral), the French Wikipedia article on the narcotrafic law, and one Public Sénat article (Nov 2024, neutral-institutional). Le Monde, Libération, the Sénat site, LR programme pages and 2026 campaign coverage were not consulted directly. The 2026 facts (candidacy on 12 Feb 2026, LR vote on 19 Apr 2026 with 73.8%, Senate re-election in 2026) rest on Wikipedia only. The legal list is empty because no case personally implicating him was found in these sources; absence is not confirmed by a court or AFP search. Mediapart's 2017 report naming him as a recipient of a EUR 3,029 Senate-group reimbursement is not a judicial case against him. Traits are empty because none could be corroborated by two sources of different leanings.
